Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the risk score levels, review days, issue target days, change limits and the phones of the managing director and the PMO lead.
Fill Projects with each project and its contingency reserve. Reserve drawn, reserve left and the open risks and issues fill in from the other sheets.

Enter each risk on Risk Register with probability and impact from 1 to 5, the cost if it occurs, an owner, a response and the next review date. Score, level, expected cost and the check fill in by themselves.
Record actions on Risk and Issue Actions, indicators on Risk Triggers and each review on Risk Reviews. Risk Heat Map counts the open risks in each cell.
Log every issue on Issue Log with severity, owner and due date. Age, target days, state and the escalation level fill in. Record each escalation on Escalations.
Log every change request on Change Requests, assess it by area on Change Impact and record the board decision on Change Board Decisions.
Write down decisions on Decision Log, assumptions on Assumptions, and what the plan needs from others on Dependencies.
Record every draw on a reserve on Contingency Drawdowns and link it to the risk that occurred.
After each phase and at the end, write lessons on Lessons Learned with an action and an owner.
Read RAID Summary every Monday: open risks, expected cost against the reserve, issues, changes, assumptions and dependencies of every project, with the items needing attention.

Use the 14 calculators for risk score, expected cost, reserve, response value, change impact, approval route, issue escalation, decision deadline, burn-down, schedule buffer, cost of delay and assumption dates.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to send one of 30 ready texts with the details already filled in. Read Risk and Change Dashboard and Charts every week.
Plan sprints, run the board and forecast the release in Excel
Plan sprints, run the board and forecast the release
Sprint capacity from days and focus
days available and the focus factor of each person give the capacity in story points, set against the points assigned, with a check for over and under capacity
Velocity of the last three sprints
points done in each closed sprint, the average of three, the trend and a warning when the velocity falls two sprints in a row
Burndown with ideal line and projection
points remaining each sprint day against the ideal line, with the projected line for the days still to come and the gap in points
Product backlog with the state of every item
every item shows if it needs an estimate or an owner, is ready, is in a sprint or is done, with the age in days and the criteria written
Board cards with days in work
each card shows its column, days in work and a flag for blocked, expedite or stale, so the oldest work is seen first
cards in each column are counted against the limit of the board, with the room left and a warning when a column is over
days from start to finish of every card, the share within your target and the cards and points finished per week
each blocker has a cause, an owner and the days open, and is marked open, open too long or resolved
items, points and finished points of each epic roll up from the backlog, with the share done and the sprints left at the project velocity
points done, points accepted by the client and points still to accept, with the feedback and the next step of each review
every action has an owner and a due date and is marked open, due soon, overdue or done, with the days late
Release plan with days to the date
each release has a target sprint, a date and a state, with the days to go and the client contact to tell
Backlog health score for every project
ready points, estimates, bug share and old blockers combine into one score from 0 to 100 and a ready or not ready verdict
Acceptance criteria with who checked them
each item carries its criteria and whether they are met, so done means the same thing for the team and the client

Hello {staff}, sprint {number} of {project} starts on {start}. You have {days} days and a capacity of {cap_points} points. Please check the items assigned to you.
Hello {staff}, you have {assigned} points in sprint {number} of {project} and a capacity of {cap_points}. Please tell the project manager which item can move.
Team member: your card is blocked
Hello {assignee}, card {card_id} ({title}) on {project} is marked blocked. Please add the blocker to the Blockers sheet and tell us what you need.
Team member: card in work too long
Hello {assignee}, card {card_id} ({title}) has been in work for {age} days. Is it still on track? Please update the board or split the card.
Hello {staff}, the stand-up of {project} is at {time}. Please bring what you did yesterday, what you plan today and any blocker.
Hello {facilitator}, the refinement session of {project} is on {date}. Please bring estimates for the items without story points.
Hello {owner}, the retrospective action "{action}" is due on {due}. Please finish it or tell us what is in the way.
Hello {assignee}, item {item_id} ({title}) has {criteria_n} acceptance criteria written. Please add the missing ones before the sprint starts.
Team member: bug assigned to you
Hello {assignee}, item {item_id} ({title}) on {project} is assigned to you with priority {priority} and {points} points. Please look at it today.
Team member: limit reached on the board
Hello {keeper}, the {lane} column of {project} holds {cards} cards against a limit of {limit}. Please finish a card before you pull a new one.
Team member: prepare the sprint demo
Hello {presenter}, the demo of sprint {number} of {project} is on {demo_date}. Please prepare the demo of the {done_pts} finished points.
Hello {pm_name}, sprint {number} of {project} shows: {state}. {done} of {committed} points are done. Please decide what to move before the end on {end}.
Hello {pm_name}, sprint {number} of {project} has {carry} points not finished. Please place them in the next sprint or the backlog.
Hello {manager}, the velocity of {project} in sprint {number} was {done} points, trend: {trend}. Please talk about it in the retrospective.
Hello {manager}, the backlog of {name} holds {ready_pts} ready points at a velocity of {velocity}: {ready_state}. Please plan a refinement session.
Project manager: blockers open too long
Hello {manager}, blockers open too long on {name}: {old_blockers}. Please help the team remove them today.
Hello {sponsor}, you are invited to the review of sprint {number} of {project} on {demo_date}. We show {done_pts} finished points. Please confirm.
Hello {sponsor}, in the review of sprint {number} of {project} the client accepted {accepted} of {done_pts} points. Next step: {next_step}.
Hello {sponsor}, at a velocity of {velocity} points the open backlog of {name} is done on {forecast_date}. Sprints left: {sprints_left}.
Hello {client_contact}, the refinement session of {project} is on {date}. Please bring your priorities so that we can order the backlog together.
Hello {client_contact}, release {release} of {project} is planned for {date}. We would like to show you the result before then. Please suggest a time.
Hello {client_contact}, points of sprint {number} of {project} waiting for your acceptance: {to_accept}. Please accept them or tell us what to change.
Client contact: work added in the sprint
Hello {client_contact}, new work in sprint {number} of {project} means something of the same size must leave. Which item should move?
Hello {client_contact}, release {release} of {project} goes out on {date}. Scope: {scope}. Please tell us if anything is missing.
Vendor: capacity for the next sprints
Hello, we plan the next sprints of {name}. How many developer days can {vendor} give from the start of the next sprint? Please answer this week.
Hello, bug {item_id} on {project} ({title}) has priority {priority}. Please send your fix date and your estimate in story points.
Hello {facilitator}, the retrospective of sprint {number} of {project} is on {held_on}. Earlier actions still open: {open_actions}. Please start with them.
PMO lead: board over its limits
Hello, the board of {name}: columns over the limit {wip_over}, blocked cards {blocked}. Please check with {manager} this week.
Sprint plan for the team and the client

Sprint {col:sprints.number} of {col:sprints.project}, ID {col:sprints.sprint_id}. Status: {col:sprints.status}. The sprint runs from {col:sprints.start} to {col:sprints.end}. Project manager: {col:sprints.pm_name}.

The team commits {col:sprints.committed} story points against a capacity of {col:sprints.capacity} points. In the backlog {col:sprints.assigned} points are assigned to this sprint. The commitment check shows: {col:sprints.commit_check}.
A plan above {set:over_pct} of the capacity needs work taken out before the sprint starts. A plan below {set:under_pct} leaves room for another item from the ready backlog.
An item enters the sprint only with an estimate, an owner and acceptance criteria. New work enters during the sprint only when something of the same size leaves it.
Sprint review summary for the sponsor and the client
Project: {col:reviews.project}. Sprint {col:reviews.number}, review on {col:reviews.demo_date}. Presented by {col:reviews.presenter}.

The team committed {col:reviews.committed} story points and finished {col:reviews.done_pts}. The client accepted {col:reviews.accepted} points, so {col:reviews.to_accept} points still wait for acceptance. The state of the acceptance is: {col:reviews.state}.
Feedback of the client: {col:reviews.feedback}. Next step: {col:reviews.next_step}.
Sponsor: {col:reviews.sponsor}. Client contact: {col:reviews.client_contact}. Points are accepted when every acceptance criterion of the item is met.
Please send any change request before the next sprint planning, so that we can size it and place it in the backlog.
Velocity and forecast report for a project
Velocity and forecast report of {set:firm}, dated {today}.

The average velocity of the last three closed sprints is {col:projects.velocity} story points. The backlog holds {col:projects.points_open} open points in {col:projects.items_open} items, of which {col:projects.ready_pts} points are ready.

Sprints left at this velocity: {col:projects.sprints_left}. The open backlog is done on {col:projects.forecast_date}. The active sprint is number {col:projects.sprint_no} and its state is: {col:projects.sprint_state}.
The forecast moves when the velocity or the scope changes. We review it at every sprint review and tell the sponsor when the date moves.
Product backlog summary for the client contact

The backlog holds {col:projects.items_open} open items worth {col:projects.points_open} story points. {col:projects.ready_pts} points are ready to start and {col:projects.unest} items still need an estimate.

Bugs make up {col:projects.bug_pct} of the open items ({col:projects.bugs_open} bugs). The bug check shows: {col:projects.bug_check}. The state of the backlog for the next sprints is: {col:projects.ready_state}.
We ask the client contact to confirm the order of the items before each sprint planning. Items without an estimate are discussed in the next refinement session.
Release notes for users and the client
The release is planned for sprint {col:releases.sprint_no} ({col:releases.target_sprint}). The state against its date is: {col:releases.state}.
Please test the points above and tell {col:releases.client_contact} or the project manager of any problem within the first days of use. Known problems are recorded as bugs in the product backlog.
The mood score of the team was {col:retros.mood} out of 5 and the check shows: {col:retros.mood_check}. {col:retros.open_actions} actions of this sprint are still open.
Each action has one owner and a due date on the Retrospective Actions sheet. We look at the open actions first at the next retrospective.
Stand-up record of one person and day
A blocker with an owner goes on the Blockers sheet the same day. The project manager checks every open blocker at the next stand-up.
Project: {col:projects.name}. Project manager: {col:projects.manager}. Active sprint: number {col:projects.sprint_no}, {col:projects.sprint_state}.
On the board {col:projects.c_ready} cards are in Ready, {col:projects.c_prog} in progress, {col:projects.c_review} in review and {col:projects.c_done} are done.
Cards blocked: {col:projects.blocked}. Blockers open too long: {col:projects.old_blockers}. Columns over their work-in-progress limit: {col:projects.wip_over}.
A column over its limit stops new work until a card moves on. We start with the oldest blocked card at the next stand-up.
Epic status note for the client

The epic holds {col:epics.items} items worth {col:epics.points} story points. {col:epics.done_pts} points are finished and {col:epics.left_pts} points are left, so {col:epics.pct} is done. The state is: {col:epics.state}.
Sprints still needed if the epic gets all of the velocity of the project: {col:epics.sprints_needed}. When other epics run at the same time it takes longer.
We discuss the order of the epics with the client contact at every sprint review.
